page: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v7 is a compute-focused instance within the Dlsv7 family, configured with 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, the CPU features dedicated thread allocation with two threads per core. The processor incorporates an extensive 480 MB L3 cache, complemented by 2 MB of L2 cache and 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, alongside architectural extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix acceleration instructions.

The instance is provisioned with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-dense 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation. It does not bundle local disk storage, requiring external Azure network-attached storage volumes for persistent data, and includes zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show strong compute performance, recording a PassMark CPU score of 66066.16 with particular strength in extended vector instructions and cryptographic tasks. Memory throughput demonstrates 173.98 GB/sec in large uncached reads and 68.56 GB/sec in writes, while cached small-block operations achieve 3532.24 GB/sec.

Throughput-intensive operations show marked strengths, including 75.36 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks, 79.02 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads, and strong compression decompression metrics exceeding 303 GB/sec in multithreaded bzip3. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides an efficient hardware allocation for workloads that demand substantial raw processor power without paying for unneeded memory capacity.

Because the server lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, it is constrained in disk-heavy caching and hardware-accelerated machine learning training. However, the high core count and vector extensions make Microsoft Azure D48ls_v7 well suited for web serving fleets, CPU-based inference pipelines, batch compression, CI/CD compilation, and distributed database operations.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v7 is a compute-oriented virtual machine powered by a 48-vCPU Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz across 24 physical cores on the x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 96.0 GB of RAM, the system delivers a lean 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio tailored for CPU-bound applications. The architecture incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, backed by a large 480 MB L3 cache. There are no attached local storage drives or discrete GPUs, making persistent workloads reliant on remote storage. Benchmarks highlight upper-quartile execution in PassMark CPU tests, cryptographic processing, static web serving throughput reaching 75.36 GB/sec, and high-frequency in-memory database operations. Consequently, the D48ls_v7 delivers balanced compute efficiency for parallel build pipelines, web serving clusters, batch compression routines, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks.
